problems.problem: The reading ends on Israel acknowledging ‘the lot’, but the context clause never says Achan was taken by lot (it says only ‘singled out’), so the reader meets ‘the lot’ with no antecedent; and ‘so that his death atone ... and Israel acknowledge’ reads as a stiff, half-finished subjunctive at six in the morning.
problems.fix: Name the lot in the context clause and smooth the purpose clause within Radak’s words (confession for atonement, and so that Israel would own the lot true), for example: “Joshua addresses Achan, taken by lot as the thief of the devoted thing, before he and all he has are stoned and burned; Radak, on 7:19, reads the plea as asking confession so that his death might atone for his sin and Israel own the lot true.” Recount to 45 words or fewer and rerun entry-check.

problems.problem: The reading’s image is left without its point: Rashi’s reading turns on the Hebrew word behind ‘stand thou still’ meaning ‘be silent’, but the sentence never says so, so ‘silencing the sun’s song’ arrives unexplained, and ‘and so its motion, Joshua singing instead’ is a knotted run of appositions; the context clause’s ‘later killed, as are all souls in the cities taken’ is also awkward.
problems.fix: Keep Rashi’s two readings but give the hinge, for example: “Joshua speaks as Israel routs five kings, later killed with every soul in the cities taken; Rashi, on 10:12, hears the word for ‘stand thou still’ as ‘be silent’: the sun, singing as it moves, falls silent and so stands, Joshua singing in its place, and by the plain sense as ‘wait’.” Adjust punctuation to keep exactly one semicolon (replace the colon construction with a comma or ‘so that’), stay at 45 words or fewer, and rerun entry-check.
